standard.title: Bicycle Steering Head Assembly — Specification (Second Revision)
standard.description: This standard specifies the requirements for materials, dimensions, tolerances, quality, and testing of steering head assemblies used in bicycles. It unifies the requirements for both PH-type (Phillips Type) and R-type (Raleigh Type) steering head assemblies to ensure safety, steering control, and component interchangeability.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the requirements for materials, dimensions, tolerances, quality, and testing of steering head assemblies used in bicycles. It unifies the requirements for both PH-type (Phillips Type) and R-type (Raleigh Type) steering head assemblies to ensure safety, steering control, and component interchangeability.

certification.description: Voluntary Quality and Performance Specification. Unlike safety-critical complete bicycles or automotive tires under mandatory Quality Control Orders (QCOs), bicycle steering head assemblies under IS 2973:2017 are certified on a voluntary basis. Manufacturers are eligible to apply for a BIS license to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on bulk boxes or individual unit packaging. However, compliance with this specification is universally required by major national bicycle brands and government/military supply tenders to ensure standard steering clearances and bearing durability.
requirements: Conforming steering head assemblies may be stamped or marked on their packaging with the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).

The steering head assembly must comprise a unified kit of six distinct parts: 1) Lock Nut, 2) Lock Washer, 3) Adjusting Cup (Top Cup), 4) Top Cone, 5) Bottom Cup, and 6) Bottom Cone (Crown Race), working in conjunction with standard steel bearing balls.

Component bodies must be manufactured from carbon steel or low-alloy case-hardening steel. Cups and cones must be case-carburized, hardened, and tempered to resist frictional pitting and bearing wear.

The bearing ball race tracks of the cups and cones must satisfy a high surface hardness limit. The hardness of the active track surface must not be less than 55 HRC (or 600 HV) to prevent ball indentations under shock loading.

The internal threads of the lock nut and adjusting cup must be precisely formed to match standard bicycle steerer dimensions: 1 inch diameter x 24 threads per inch (25.4 mm x 1.058 mm pitch), ensuring smooth engagement without excessive backlash or binding.

To prevent atmospheric rust, components must be nickel-chromium electroplated per IS 1068 (minimum service grade No. 1 or 2) or chemically coloured/black-phosphated. Electroplated parts must be bright and free from peeling, blisters, or bare spots.

When assembled onto a standard frame and fork, the steering head must allow completely free, zero-play rotation of the handle bars without binding. It must survive on-road dynamic durability tests without losing alignment, cracking, or showing bearing race spalling.
